la:adj:mediocris.html:
mĕdĭō^cris, e (ō usually; rarely ŏ), adj.
medius
,
in a middle state between too much and too little, middling, moderate, tolerable, ordinary; sometimes also, not remarkable, indifferent, mediocre.
In gen. (class.).
Lit., of size, quantity, degree, etc., in material things: castellum,: spatium,: agmen,: intervallum,.—
Of mind, character, ability, acts, achievements, etc.: C. L. Memmii fuerunt oratores mediocres,: L. Cotta in mediocrium oratorum numero,: non mediocres viri, sed maximi et docti,: homines,: vir,: poëta,: in mediocribus vel studiis vel officiis,: amicitia,: malum,: artes,: eloquentia,: ingenium,: excusare ... mediocris est animi,narrow, small,: ut mediocris jacturae te mergat onus,.—
Esp.
Per litoten, with non (haud, nec), not insignificant, not common or trivial: Jugurthae non mediocrem animum pollicitando accendebant,i. e. ardent, ambitious,: non mediocris hominis haec sunt officia,: haud mediocris hic, ut ego quidem intellego, vir fuit,: nec mediocre

telum ad res gerendas, : non mediocrem sibi diligentiam adhibendam intellegebat,uncommon, extraordinary,: praemium non mediocre,: non mediocris dissensio, et saep.—*

With syllaba, common = anceps: syllabarum longarum et brevium et mediocrium junctura,.—Hence, adv.: mĕdĭō^crĭ-ter.
Moderately, tolerably, ordinarily, not particularly, not very, not remarkably, not much (class.): ordo annalium mediocriter nos retinet,: corpus mediocriter aegrum,.—
By litotes, with haud, ne, non (cf.: supra, mediocris, II. A.): flagitium, et damnum haud mediocriter,: non mediocriter,in no moderate degree,: reprehensus est non mediocriter,i. e. greatly, exceedingly, very much,; so ; ; —
Very little: ne mediocriter quidem disertus,not in the least,.—
With moderation, calmly, tranquilly = modice (rare, and perh. only in Cic.): quod mihi non mediocriter ferendum videtur,.— Comp.: hoc vellem mediocrius,.

la:adj:medius.gloss: middle, mid, central, between, midway between, in the center
senses: middle, mid, central, between, midway between, in the center
the middle of, the midst of
la:adj:medius.html:
mĕdĭus, a, um, adj.
Sanscr. madhya, the same; Gr. μέσος; Angl. - Sax. midd; Germ. Mitte; cf. dimidius, meridies (medi-), etc.
,
that is in the middle or midst, mid, middle (class.).
Adj.
Lit.: terra complexa medium mundi locum,; cf. : medium mundi locum petere,: versus aeque prima, et media, et extrema pars attenditur,: ultimum, proximum, medium tempus,: in foro medio,in the midst of the forum,; ; cf.: medio foro,in the open forum,: in solio medius consedit,sat in the middle,; : considit scopulo medius,: concilio medius sedebat,: ignes,: medio tempore,in the meantime, meanwhile,: vinum novum, vetus, medium, i. e. neither old nor new, Varr. ap. : cum plenus fluctu medius foret alveus,full to the middle,.—With dat.: Peloponnesii Megaram, mediam Corintho Athenisque urbem, condidere,midway between Corinth and Athens,.—With abl.: si medius Polluce et Castore ponar,between,.—With inter: cum inter bellum et pacem medium nihil sit,there is no medium, no middle course between,: inter quos numeros duo medii inveniuntur (sc. numeri),.—With gen.: locus medius regionum earum,half-way between,: locus medius juguli summique lacerti,between,; : et medius juvenum ibat,: medius silentūm,.—With ex: medius ex tribus,: medium arripere aliquem,to seize one by the middle, around the body,: juvenem medium complectitur,: Alcides medium tenuit,held him fast by the middle,: medium ostendere unguem,to point with the middle finger,.—
Transf., half (ante- and postclass.): hieme demunt cibum medium,half their food,: scrupulum croci,: aurum ... Italicis totum, medium provincialibus reddidit, Capitol. Anton. Pius, 4 fin.—
Trop., of the middle, not very great or small, middling, medial, moderate.
Of age: aetatis mediae vir,of middle age,.—
Of plans, purposes, etc.: nihil medium, nec spem nec curam, sed immensa omnia volventes animo,: medium quiddam tenere,.—
Of intellect: eloquentiā medius,middling, tolerable,: ingenium,moderate,.—
Undetermined, undecided: medios esse,i. e. neutral,: medium se gerere,: se dubium mediumque partibus praestitit,; cf.: responsum,indefinite, ambiguous,: vocabula, that can be taken in agood or bad sense, ambiguous, . —
Indifferent, not imperative: officium, a duty which is not distinctly enjoined by the moral law, but is sustained by preponderant reasoning: medium officium id esse dicunt (Graeci) quod cur factum sit, ratio probabilis reddi possit,; cf.: ex quo intellegitur, officium medium quiddam esse, quod neque in bonis ponatur neque in contrariis,; cf. sqq. and Madv. ad loc.: artes,which in themselves are neither good nor bad, indifferent,.—
Intermediate: medium erat in Anco ingenium, et Numae et Romuli memor,of a middle kind, resembling each in some degree,: nihil habet ista res (actoris) medium, sed aut lacrimas meretur aut risum,: ille jam paene medius adfectus est ex amoribus et desideriis amicorum,.—Hence, as subst.: mĕdĭus, i, m., one who stands or comes between, a mediator: medium sese offert,as a mediator,: pacator mediusque Syphax,: pacis eras mediusque belli,arbiter,; cf.: nunc mediis subeant irrita verba deis,oaths in which the gods were called upon to be mediators,.—
Central, with ex or in: ex factione media consul,fully committed to it,; so (nearly = intimus), viros fortīs et magnanimos eosdem bonos et simplicīs ... esse volumus: quae sunt ex media laude justititiae,these qualities are clearly among those which make uprightness praiseworthy,: partitiones oratoriae, quae e media illa nostra Academia effloruerunt,: ingressio e media philosophia repetita est,; : in medio maerore et dolore,; : in media dimicatione,the hottest of the fight,; cf.: in medio ardore certaminis,: in media solitudine,the most profound,: in mediis divitiis,in abundant wealth,: in medio robore virium,: in medio ardore belli,: in media reipublicae luce,the full blaze of public life,: media inter pocula,.—Hence,
Subst.: mĕdĭum, ii, n., the middle, midst.
Lit.
Of space (very rare in Cic.): in medio aedium sedens,: maris,; for which, without in, medio aedium eburneis sellis sedere, : medio viae ponere,: in agmine in primis modo, modo in postremis, saepe in medio adesse,; for which, without in, medio sextam legionem constituit, : medio montium porrigitur planities,: medio stans hostia ad aras,: medio tutissimus ibis,: in medium geminos immani pondere caestus Projecit,: in medium sarcinas coniciunt,; : equitatus consulem in medium acceptum, armis protegens, in castra reduxit,.— Trop.: tamquam arbiter honorarius medium ferire voluisse,to cut through the middle,: intacta invidiā media sunt, ad summa ferme tendit,.—
Of time: diei,: medio temporis,in the meantime, meanwhile,; cf.: nec longum in medio tempus, cum,the interval,; ; .—
Transf.
The midst of all, the presence of all, the public, the community (class.): in medio omnibus palma est posita, qui artem tractant musicam,lies open to all,: tabulae sunt in medio,: rem totam in medio ponere,publicly,, § 29: ponam in medio sententias philosophorum,: dicendi ratio in medio posita,lies open to all,: rem in medium proferre,to publish, make known,: vocare in medium, before the public, before a public tribunal: rem in medium vocare coeperunt,: in medio relinquere,to leave it to the public, leave it undecided,; : pellere e medio, to expel, reject, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 272 Vahl.); : cum jacentia verba sustulimus e medio,adopt words from the people, common words,; cf.: munda sed e medio consuetaque verba puellae Scribite, : tollere de medio, to do away with, abolish: litteras,: tollere de medio, to put out of the way, cut off, destroy: hominem,: de medio removere,to put out of sight,: e medio excedere or abire, to leave the world, to die: e medio excessit,she is dead,: ea mortem obiit, e medio abiit,: tollite lumen e medio,: recedere de medio, to go away, retire, withdraw: cur te mihi offers? recede de medio,: in medio esse,to be present,: in medium venire or procedere,to appear, come forward, show one's self in public,: in medium, before the public, for the public, for the community: communes utilitates in medium afferre,: consulere in medium,to care for the public good, for the good of all,; so opp. separantem suas res a publicis,; : quaerere,to make acquisitions for the use of all,: cedere, to fall or devolve to the community, : conferre laudem,i. e. so that all may have a share of it,: dare,to communicate for the use of all,: in medium conferre, in gaming,to put down, put in the pool,: in medio, for sub dio, in the open air: scorpios fugari posse, si aliqui ex eis urantur in medio,.—
A half (ante-class. and post-Aug.): scillae medium conterunt cum aqua,: scrobem ad medium completo,.—Hence,
Adv.: mĕdĭē, in the middle, in a middling degree, moderately, tolerably (except once in Tac. only post-class.): qui noluerant medie,kept quiet, remained neutral,: nec plane optimi, nec oppido deterrimi sunt, sed quasi medie morati,; ; : ortus medie humilis,.—
Indefinitely, .

la:adj:medicinus.gloss: Of or pertaining to doctors and healing; medical, medicinal
senses: Of or pertaining to doctors and healing; medical, medicinal
la:adj:medicinus.html:
mĕdĭcīnus, a, um, adj.
1. medicus
,
of or belonging to a physician or surgeon, medical (as adj. only ante- and post-class.; as subst. class.).
Adj.: ars,the healing art, medicine, Müll.; ; .—
Subst.: mĕdĭcīna, ae, f.
(Sc. ars.) The healing or medical art, medicine, surgery: ut medicina (ars est) valetudinis,; : medicina, quae ex observatione salubrium atque his contrariorum reperta est,: tertiam esse partem medicinae, quae manu curet, i. e. surgery, Cels. prooem. 7: medicinam excolere,: exercere,: facere,: factitare,to practise,: clarus medicinā,.—
(Sc. officina.) The shop of a physician or surgeon; the booth in which a physician waited on his patients and vended his medicines (rare; not in Cic.): in medicinis, in tonstrinis,; cf.: veteres absolute dicebant pistrinam et sutrinam et medicinam, Don. , 2, 45 (the taberna of the physician is mentioned in ).—
(Sc. res.) A remedy, medicine.
Lit.: si medicus veniat, qui huic morbo facere medicinam potest,i. e. heal, cure,: accipere medicinam,.—
Transf. *
Like medicamentum, poison, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 579 Rib.).—
The pruning of vines, .—
Trop., a remedy, relief, antidote (a favorite word of Cic.): singulis medicinam consilii atque orationis meae afferam,: sed non egeo medicinā: me ipse consolor,: sublevatio et medicina,: temporis,: doloris,: laboris,: calamitatis,: quae sanaret vitiosas partes rei publicae,: crede mihi, non ulla tua'st medicina figurae,i. e. no means of rendering beautiful,: periculorum,: malorum,: curae,.—In plur.: his quatuor causis totidem medicinae opponuntur,.

senses: practice or art of medicine or healing

mĕdĭcus, a, um
medeor
,
of or pertaining to healing, healing, curative, medical (as adj., poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Adj.: medicas adhibere manus ad vulnera,: ars,: potus,: vis,: salubritas,: usus,: digitus, the next to the little finger (cf. medicinalis), . —*
Transf., magical: Marmaridae, medicum vulgus, ad quorum tactum mites jacuere cerastae,.—
Subst.:
mĕdĭcus, i, m.
A medical man, physician, surgeon (class.): medicus nobilissimus atque optimus quaeritur,: medicum arcessere,: admovere aegro,: vulnerum,a surgeon,: caeduntur tumidae medico ridente mariscae, ; cf.: medicus ait se obligasse crus fractum Aesculapio, Apollini autem bracchium,: MEDICVS CLINICVS, CHIRVRGVS, OCVLARIVS,: AVRICVLARIVS,: IVMENTARIVS,; cf.: medici pecorum,: LEGIONIS,; : DVPLARIVS TRIREMIS,: instrumentum medici,.—Prov.: medice, cura teipsum,.—
The finger next the little finger, Gr. δάκτυλος ἰατρικός, .—
mĕdĭ-ca, ae, f., a female physician (post-class.), Oud.; ; ; sq.—Also, a midwife, Interpr. ; .—
mĕdĭca, ōrum, n., medicinal herbs, .

la:verb:medeor.gloss: to heal, cure, remedy, be good for or against a disease
senses: to heal, cure, remedy, be good for or against a disease
la:verb:medeor.html:
mĕdĕor, 2,
v. dep. n. [root madh, to be wise; Zend, madha, the healing art; cf. μάθος, also medicus, re-med-ium], to heal, cure, be good for or against a disease (syn.: medico, sano, curo); constr. with dat., rarely with contra, very rarely with acc. (class.).
Lit.
Of pers. subjects: medico non solum morbus ejus, cui mederi volet, cognoscendus est,.—Prov.: cum capiti mederi debeam, reduviam curo,i. e. to neglect matters of importance while attending to trifles,.—
Of subjects not personal: contra serpentium ictus mederi,: oculis herba chelidonia,: dolori dentium,: capitis vulneribus,: medendi ars,the healing art, art of medicine,; ; —Pass.: ut ex vino stomachi dolor medeatur,; cf.: medendae valetudini leniendisque morbis opem adhibere,.—
Trop., to remedy, relieve, amend, correct, restore, etc.
With dat.: huic malo,: dies stultis quoque mederi solet,: incommodis omnium,: afflictae et perditae rei publicae,: religioni,: inopiae rei frumentariae,: tum satietati, tum ignorantiae lectorum,to provide against,: rei alicui lege aut decreto senatus,.—
With acc.: quas (cupiditates) mederi possis,; .—Pass.: aquae medendis corporibus nobiles,.—Absol.: aegrescit medendo,his disorder increases with the remedy,.—Impers. pass.: ut huic vitio medeatur,.—Hence, mĕdens, entis (gen. plur. medentum, ), subst., a physician (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): veluti pueris absinthia tetra medentes cum dare conantur,; : Democrates e primis medentium,; .

la:verb:meditor.gloss: to think or reflect upon, consider, contemplate, ponder, meditate (upon); intend
senses: to think or reflect upon, consider, contemplate, ponder, meditate (upon); intend
to meditate, study, exercise oneself in, practise or rehearse something
la:verb:meditor.html:
mĕdĭtor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. a. and n.
Sanscr. madh-a, wisdom; Gr. μάθος, μανθάνω, μήδομαι; cf.: medeor, re-med-ium, etc.
; act., to think or reflect upon, to muse over, consider, meditate upon; neutr., to think, reflect, muse, consider, meditate; to design, purpose, intend, etc.; constr. with acc., with ad, de, with dat., with inf., with a rel.-clause, or absol. (class.).
Lit.
With acc.: semulque cursuram meditabor ad ludos Olympios,: ea para, meditare, cogita, quae, etc.,: nihil aliud cogitare, meditari, curare nisi, etc.,: forum, subsellia, rostra curiamque,: fugam ad legiones,: cor tuum meditabitur timorem,i. e. promote by meditation,.—
With ad; ne ad eam rem meditere, : ad hujus vitae studium meditati illi sunt qui feruntur labores tui,.—
With de: ut de tua ratione meditere,.—
With dat. (ante-class.): nugis,. —(ε) With inf.: jam designatus alio incessu esse meditabatur,: multos annos regnare meditatus magno labore,: cum animo meditaretur proficisci in Persas,.— (ζ) With a rel.-clause: ea nunc meditabor quo modo illi dicam,: meditabor, quo modo cum illo loquar,: quid contra dicerem, mecum ipse meditabor,: meditare, quibus verbis incensam illius cupiditatem comprimas,.— (η) Absol.: multis modis meditatus egomet mecum sum,: egressus ad meditandum in agro,. —
Transf., to meditate, study, exercise one's self in, practise a thing: nugas est meditatus male,: Demosthenes perfecit meditando, ut nemo planius esse locutus putaretur,; cf.: Demosthenes in litore meditans,: quid Crassus ageret meditandi aut discendi causā,: aut in foro dicere aut meditari extra forum,: musam,: arma,: proelia,.—Transf., of animals: cervi editos partus exercent cursu, et fugam meditari docent,to practise flight,.—Of things: semper cauda scorpionis in ictu est: nulloque momento meditari cessat, to move as in readiness to strike, i. e. to threaten, : semina meditantur aristas,; also, to murmur, utter a sad cry: clamabo, meditabor ut columba,; .—
In pass. signif. (in verb. fin. post-class. and very rare): adulteria meditantur,.—But freq. in part. perf.: mĕdĭtā-tus, a, um.
Exercised, practised, instructed (only Plautin.): cumque huc ad adulescentem meditatum probe mittam,: probe meditatam utramque duco,: murmura,.—
Thought upon, meditated, weighed, considered, studied: meditati sunt doli docte,: ea, quae meditata et praeparata inferuntur,: meditatum et cogitatum scelus,: meditatum cogitatumque verbum,: accuratae et meditatae commentationes,: oratio,: doli,: meditata et composita oratio (opp. extemporized), . —Subst.: mĕdĭtāta, ōrum, n., a carefully prepared speech: sive meditata sive subita proferret,.—Hence, adv.: mĕdĭtātē, thoughtfully, designedly, intentionally (ante-class. and post-Aug.): ne tu illorum mores perquam meditate tenes,knowest thoroughly,: hau male meditate male dicax es,: effundere probra,.

la:verb:medico.html:
mĕdĭco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
1. medicus
,
to heal, cure (poet. and in post-Aug. prose for the class. medeor).
Lit.
With acc.: ego istum lepide medicabo metum,: (apes) odore galbani,: vulneris aestus,: furores,.—
With dat.: tremulis membris,.—
Transf.
To impart the virtue of a remedy, give healing power to: hoc fusum labris splendentibus amnem Inficit, occulte medicans,.—
To besprinkle with the juice of herbs, to medicate: semina,to steep,: semina omnia suco herbae quae sedum appellatur, medicare,: exigua portione medicatur aqua,; : vinum medicatum,i. e. spurious, adulterated,: merum,: ficus,.
To color, dye, with tingere: capillos,.—Hence, mĕdĭcātus, a, um, P. a.
Besprinkled with juices, sprinkled, medicated (poet. and post-Aug.): semina suco herbae sedi,: sedes,places sprinkled with the juice of herbs,: somnus, produced by a juice or a charm, : fruges,: lana medicata fuco,stained, dyed,: Amyclaeis medicatum vellus ahenis,.—To poison: boletum medicatum,i. e. poisoned,: herbae,; cf.: medicata veneno tela,: medicatae cuspidis ictus,: mortui,embalmed,.—
Useful or good for healing, medicinal: aquae medicatae,: sapor aquae,: fontes,; ; : potio,: inguen,.—Comp.: lac bubulum medicatius,.—Sup.: res medicatissimae,.

senses: as the subjective location of the intense inner physical sensation of a heightened emotion, such as erotic passion
la:noun:medulla.html:
mĕdulla, ae, f.
medius
,
the marrow of bones; the pith of plants (class.).
Lit., : cumque albis ossa medullis,: ossa regum vacuis exsucta medullis,: per media foramina a cerebro medullā descendente,.—
Transf., the pith, inside, kernel: vitis medullā,; : frumenta, quae salsā aquā sparsa moluntur, candidiorem medullam reddunt,i. e. meal, flour,: medulla ventris,the inside,.—
Trop., the marrow, kernel, innermost part, best part, quintessence: at ego pereo, cui medullam lassitudo perbibit,: cum hic fervor tamquam in venis medullisque insederit,; cf.: in medullis populi Romani ac visceribus haerebant,: haec mihi semper erunt imis infixa medullis,: qui mihi haeres in medullis,who are at the bottom of my heart,:

qui mihi sunt inclusa medullis, : nondum implevere medullas maturae mala nequitiae,: communes loci, qui in mediis litium medullis versantur,: verborum,inner meaning,: divisio compagum ac medullarum,the innermost parts,.—Poet.: suadae, the marrow or quintessence of eloquence, said of Cethegus, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 309 Vahl.); cf. .

Adj.
Lit.: terra complexa medium mundi locum,; cf. : medium mundi locum petere,: versus aeque prima, et media, et extrema pars attenditur,: ultimum, proximum, medium tempus,: in foro medio,in the midst of the forum,; ; cf.: medio foro,in the open forum,: in solio medius consedit,sat in the middle,; : considit scopulo medius,: concilio medius sedebat,: ignes,: medio tempore,in the meantime, meanwhile,: vinum novum, vetus, medium, i. e. neither old nor new, Varr. ap. : cum plenus fluctu medius foret alveus,full to the middle,.—With dat.: Peloponnesii Megaram, mediam Corintho Athenisque urbem, condidere,midway between Corinth and Athens,.—With abl.: si medius Polluce et Castore ponar,between,.—With inter: cum inter bellum et pacem medium nihil sit,there is no medium, no middle course between,: inter quos numeros duo medii inveniuntur (sc. numeri),.—With gen.: locus medius regionum earum,half-way between,: locus medius juguli summique lacerti,between,; : et medius juvenum ibat,: medius silentūm,.—With ex: medius ex tribus,: medium arripere aliquem,to seize one by the middle, around the body,: juvenem medium complectitur,: Alcides medium tenuit,held him fast by the middle,: medium ostendere unguem,to point with the middle finger,.—
Transf., half (ante- and postclass.): hieme demunt cibum medium,half their food,: scrupulum croci,: aurum ... Italicis totum, medium provincialibus reddidit, Capitol. Anton. Pius, 4 fin.—
Trop., of the middle, not very great or small, middling, medial, moderate.
Of age: aetatis mediae vir,of middle age,.—
Of plans, purposes, etc.: nihil medium, nec spem nec curam, sed immensa omnia volventes animo,: medium quiddam tenere,.—
Of intellect: eloquentiā medius,middling, tolerable,: ingenium,moderate,.—
Undetermined, undecided: medios esse,i. e. neutral,: medium se gerere,: se dubium mediumque partibus praestitit,; cf.: responsum,indefinite, ambiguous,: vocabula, that can be taken in agood or bad sense, ambiguous, . —
Indifferent, not imperative: officium, a duty which is not distinctly enjoined by the moral law, but is sustained by preponderant reasoning: medium officium id esse dicunt (Graeci) quod cur factum sit, ratio probabilis reddi possit,; cf.: ex quo intellegitur, officium medium quiddam esse, quod neque in bonis ponatur neque in contrariis,; cf. sqq. and Madv. ad loc.: artes,which in themselves are neither good nor bad, indifferent,.—
Intermediate: medium erat in Anco ingenium, et Numae et Romuli memor,of a middle kind, resembling each in some degree,: nihil habet ista res (actoris) medium, sed aut lacrimas meretur aut risum,: ille jam paene medius adfectus est ex amoribus et desideriis amicorum,.—Hence, as subst.: mĕdĭus, i, m., one who stands or comes between, a mediator: medium sese offert,as a mediator,: pacator mediusque Syphax,: pacis eras mediusque belli,arbiter,; cf.: nunc mediis subeant irrita verba deis,oaths in which the gods were called upon to be mediators,.—
Central, with ex or in: ex factione media consul,fully committed to it,; so (nearly = intimus), viros fortīs et magnanimos eosdem bonos et simplicīs ... esse volumus: quae sunt ex media laude justititiae,these qualities are clearly among those which make uprightness praiseworthy,: partitiones oratoriae, quae e media illa nostra Academia effloruerunt,: ingressio e media philosophia repetita est,; : in medio maerore et dolore,; : in media dimicatione,the hottest of the fight,; cf.: in medio ardore certaminis,: in media solitudine,the most profound,: in mediis divitiis,in abundant wealth,: in medio robore virium,: in medio ardore belli,: in media reipublicae luce,the full blaze of public life,: media inter pocula,.—Hence,
Subst.: mĕdĭum, ii, n., the middle, midst.
Lit.
Of space (very rare in Cic.): in medio aedium sedens,: maris,; for which, without in, medio aedium eburneis sellis sedere, : medio viae ponere,: in agmine in primis modo, modo in postremis, saepe in medio adesse,; for which, without in, medio sextam legionem constituit, : medio montium porrigitur planities,: medio stans hostia ad aras,: medio tutissimus ibis,: in medium geminos immani pondere caestus Projecit,: in medium sarcinas coniciunt,; : equitatus consulem in medium acceptum, armis protegens, in castra reduxit,.— Trop.: tamquam arbiter honorarius medium ferire voluisse,to cut through the middle,: intacta invidiā media sunt, ad summa ferme tendit,.—
Of time: diei,: medio temporis,in the meantime, meanwhile,; cf.: nec longum in medio tempus, cum,the interval,; ; .—
Transf.
The midst of all, the presence of all, the public, the community (class.): in medio omnibus palma est posita, qui artem tractant musicam,lies open to all,: tabulae sunt in medio,: rem totam in medio ponere,publicly,, § 29: ponam in medio sententias philosophorum,: dicendi ratio in medio posita,lies open to all,: rem in medium proferre,to publish, make known,: vocare in medium, before the public, before a public tribunal: rem in medium vocare coeperunt,: in medio relinquere,to leave it to the public, leave it undecided,; : pellere e medio, to expel, reject, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 272 Vahl.); : cum jacentia verba sustulimus e medio,adopt words from the people, common words,; cf.: munda sed e medio consuetaque verba puellae Scribite, : tollere de medio, to do away with, abolish: litteras,: tollere de medio, to put out of the way, cut off, destroy: hominem,: de medio removere,to put out of sight,: e medio excedere or abire, to leave the world, to die: e medio excessit,she is dead,: ea mortem obiit, e medio abiit,: tollite lumen e medio,: recedere de medio, to go away, retire, withdraw: cur te mihi offers? recede de medio,: in medio esse,to be present,: in medium venire or procedere,to appear, come forward, show one's self in public,: in medium, before the public, for the public, for the community: communes utilitates in medium afferre,: consulere in medium,to care for the public good, for the good of all,; so opp. separantem suas res a publicis,; : quaerere,to make acquisitions for the use of all,: cedere, to fall or devolve to the community, : conferre laudem,i. e. so that all may have a share of it,: dare,to communicate for the use of all,: in medium conferre, in gaming,to put down, put in the pool,: in medio, for sub dio, in the open air: scorpios fugari posse, si aliqui ex eis urantur in medio,.—
A half (ante-class. and post-Aug.): scillae medium conterunt cum aqua,: scrobem ad medium completo,.—Hence,
Adv.: mĕdĭē, in the middle, in a middling degree, moderately, tolerably (except once in Tac. only post-class.): qui noluerant medie,kept quiet, remained neutral,: nec plane optimi, nec oppido deterrimi sunt, sed quasi medie morati,; ; : ortus medie humilis,.—
Indefinitely, .

la:other:Medea.html:
Mēdēa, ae (arch.
gen. Medeaï, Enn. ap. ; v. Vahl.; nom.Mēdē, acc. to Vahl.), and Mēdīa, f., = Μήδεια, a celebrated sorceress, daughter of Æetes, king of Colchis. She assisted her lover, Jason the Argonaut, in obtaining the golden fleece, accompanied him to Greece, and prevented her father, who was in pursuit, from overtaking them, by strewing the sea with her brother's limbs. When Jason afterwards repudiated her, in order to marry Creusa, she killed the children she had had by him, and burned the bride to death in her palace: item ut Medea Peliam concoxit senem,; sqq.; : ne pueros coram populo Medea trucidet,.—The subject of tragedies by several authors, v. .—
Transf.
Medea Palatina, i. e. Clodia, .—
Medea nigra, a precious stone, so named after Medea, .—Hence,
Mēdēis, ĭdis, f.adj., Medean, magical (poet.): Medeides herbae,.
